q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of cheese per kg?
title: Cheese carbon footprint per kg
short: Most of cheese comes from the milk: multiply the litres of milk per kg of cheese by the milk's farm figure, then add pasteurising, cooking, pressing, ripening and cold store energy. Divide the plant's energy by kg of cheese made.

ul: Litres of milk per kg of cheese, often around ten for hard cheese.
Whey sold or used, which can share the milk footprint.
Pasteurising and cheese vats, heated by steam.

p: Report per kg by cheese type, and say how the milk footprint is split between cheese and whey.

example.title: Worked example: cheese unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 59,000 / 50,000 = 1.180 kg CO2 per kg
Add milk for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
